answer: In this PoA design, identity verification requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result is the input to the next and a Wesolowski proof certifies correct elapsed work. An attacker may create many apparent clones, but cannot parallelize any single chain across GPUs to reduce its physical delay; each clone therefore consumes an independent time bottleneck. The tide of valid identities remains bounded, while prism and crystal serve as protocol-bound labels, not shortcuts.
